newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Bulls continue to run rampant on Zimbabwe bourse.
newsitem.headline: Bulls continue to run rampant on Zimbabwe bourse.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks continued their bullrun on Friday with brokers saying the current buying momentum could see the main industrial index scaling the key 10,000 pyschological peak in the coming week.
The 57-share index soared 200.41 points -- a rise of 2.1 percent -- to close Friday at an all time high of 9,831.53. It shot up 908.88 points on the week.
"I think it's time for a bit of control because this is out of control. It's scary. It's getting to a point where the market could get very, very volatile," one broker said.
"We would like the firmness to be sustained rather than going up and down sharply," he said.

The industrial index has been breaking records for the past three months, driven largely by local investors optimistic that Zimbabwe's agro-based economy was set for higher growth this year on the back of good rains.
"The index now looks set to test the 10,000 level during the coming week based on current momentum," another broker said.

In industrials on Friday, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans led the winners, soaring 800 cents to 5,800 while blue-chip beverages and supermarkets conglomerate Delta leapt 200 cents to 4,500, department stores Haddon and Sly surged 125 cents to 600.

Bankers Barclays rose 100 cents 3,100, agricultural company Acacia, pork processor Colcom and seed manufacturer and distributor SeedCo added 20 cents each to 360, 410 and 260 respectively, while packaging firm Hunyani at 365 and steel window and door-maker Radar at 410 both put on 15 cents.

A few counters bucked the trend, notably horticultural firm Ariston which dropped 100 cents to 2,400, while clothing retailer Truworths shed 30 cents to 1,280 and soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes lost 10 cents to 350.
Minings were more active than of late with copper producer Mhangura edging two cents up to 27 and gold counter Rio Tinto adding 10 cents to 2,810.
The seven-share mining index ended 1.15 points up at 1,154.57 -- a rise of 36.82 points on the week.
